tasks.short: Explain production delays, difficulties and cost estimate changes with supporting records.

steps.what: Retrieve production progress, material availability and cost records.
Collect messages explaining shortages, breakdowns and revised delivery dates.

loop.input: Messages linked to the work order.
loop.output: Dated disruption evidence with source references and unresolved claims.
loop.check: Validate order identifiers and dates; the clerk checks ambiguous causes and conflicting messages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per case; unresolved fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Messages describe causes and revised dates in varied free text.

steps.what: Ask the department supervisor to clarify causes, recovery actions and missing facts.
Compare original and revised costs and calculate the documented variance.
Write the explanation and attach supporting records.

loop.input: Confirmed explanation, calculated variance and linked evidence.
loop.output: A delay report separating confirmed facts, estimates and open questions.
loop.check: Copy numbers from validated calculations; require evidence references and clerk review of causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported explanations remain blank for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but varied evidence needs a short written explanation.

steps.what: Approve material explanations, revised estimates and report release.
File the approved report and evidence against the work order.
Send the approved explanation to the designated recipients.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins work-order records from the {OPS_SYSTEM} with estimates and costs from the {ERP}, calculates variances and assembles evidence. Two bounded loops extract relevant messages from the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} and draft a report in the {DOCS}; the clerk checks evidence and discusses unresolved causes with the department supervisor. The {WORKFLOW} records manager approval, archives the approved version and releases it through the {EMAIL} using that same approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order identifiers, estimate versions and explanations sit in separate records and messages. Joining them was costly, while cause attribution still needed discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Available exports or APIs support deterministic joins and calculations. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded extraction and drafting can handle variable text without deciding responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Late production updates, missing cost allocations and disputed causes remain difficult. GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on use, especially if the scope expands to evaluating workers. Employee consultation and approval requirements follow national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk tests explanations against practical production knowledge and asks questions people may hesitate to answer in writing. The manager judges responsibility, commercial wording and whether a revised estimate is justified.

ambition.what: Weekly review of recurring delay causes and prevention priorities

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time collecting attachments and writing reports, and more time investigating recurring disruptions. They can gain delegated authority to request missing evidence and trigger agreed escalation thresholds; estimate approval remains with the manager.

reach.task: Compare material arrival delays with production disruptions.
reach.learn: Event timestamps, lead-time variation and the difference between correlation and cause.

reach.task: Assess whether a proposed process change reduces recurring delay costs.
reach.learn: Cost allocation, baseline selection and measuring results after a change.

evidence.claim: Production clerks commonly combine operational records, supervisor explanations and cost comparisons to document disruptions.
Record joins, version comparisons, variance calculations and approval routing can use deterministic technology.
Qargo reads PDF transport orders into fields; this supports bounded extraction feasibility, not automated production-cause attribution.
The EU AI Act distinguishes worker-related employment uses from ordinary operational document processing.
The Netherlands has works-council consent rules covering certain working-time and employee-monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: This is a typical mid-size production business with separate operational and financial records.
A spreadsheet bridges cost records and estimates; some companies already perform this comparison inside the {ERP}.
Material reports receive manager approval; routine factual updates may have delegated release rules.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The prior's document-heavy pattern fits, but structured joins and calculations cover more work than its low rule-coverage estimate suggests.
The consultation range assumes a limited reporting change; formal national procedures can take longer.
The initial scope documents work orders and disruptions without scoring individual employees.
unknowns: Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} share stable work-order identifiers.
Whether original estimates and revisions are retained with timestamps.
Which causes are already recorded in structured fields.
Who approves cost changes and customer-facing explanations.
Which APIs, exports and mailbox permissions are available.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules or agreements.
Actual case volumes, handling times and evidence retention requirements.
research_questions: How often can historical reports be reconstructed from existing records without another supervisor conversation?
Which variance components reconcile reliably to the {ERP}?
Can message extraction preserve contradictory evidence and identify unsupported causal claims?
Which existing {WORKFLOW} and {DOCS} features cover approval, version locking and filing?
new_work: Review ambiguous message extraction and unsupported report claims.
Resolve unmatched work orders, stale records and missing estimate versions.
Maintain variance formulas, evidence mappings and recipient rules.
Check failed imports and releases and preserve approval records.
Review access, retention and any changes affecting employee consultation.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward investigating disruption patterns and preparing prevention proposals. Broader escalation rights require explicit delegation; managerial cost and commercial decisions remain accountable human decisions.
reach: Logistics analysis of material delays affecting production.
Management analysis of recurring disruption costs and prevention results.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly disruption review that links recurring causes, cost impact and proposed prevention actions, then tracks whether approved changes help.
